On the segment between distinct input points, positivity of DY=(I+DT)/2 gives strict monotonicity. The inverse function theorem and injectivity yield a global C¹ inverse on the open image Ω, contained in L. Differentiating W gives the stated Cayley transform, which is symmetric with eigenvalues (λ−1)/(λ+1)∈(−1,1) for λ>0.

The source inverse maps Y↦Y∓W have Jacobians I∓B. Their determinant equality follows from det DT=1 and their product is det(I−B²). Both determinants are positive. Thus η≤1 and change of variables gives mass V, while half-summing and half-differencing the zero source first moments gives both zero weighted means.

With eigenvalues β_j the AM–GM step bounds the product by (1−Σβ_j²/d)^(d/2). For d≥2 this is at most 1−Σβ_j²/d, giving the integrated estimate after splitting |L| by Ω. In d=2 equal determinants give tr B=0, hence η=1−b² and ||B||_F²=2b² pointwise.

Changing variables in the two caps yields thresholds h+u·W and −h−u·W, respectively. Both signs match the original closed cap inequalities. Boundaries of the source bodies are volume null, and the thresholds depend on the same midpoint point under the integral.
